JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries suffered by him in a road accident dated 27.02.2023.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 27.02.2023 at about 09.30pm, the Petitioner was going in his Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LH-0290 on Bannerghatta Road, near Basavanapura Bus Stop,
Bangalore and a Swift D'Zire Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AH- 4500 came at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's Scooter.
Due to the impact, the petitioner was thrown on the road and sustained sever injuries to his right leg.

3. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Medax Hospital given first aid treatment and then shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bangalore wherein he was treated as an inpatient, undergone operation.
Due to the injuries suffered in the accident, the petitioner is suffering from permanent disability and unable to continue his work.

Before the accident he was working as a "Dry Cleaner" at James Bond, B.G. Koli Form Gate,
Bangalore and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
So far he has spent Rs.75,000/- towards surgery and medical expenses, nourishment and transportation expenses.

The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending D'Zire Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AH-4500 and the Hulimavu Traffic police have filed charge sheet against the driver in Cr.No.28/2022 punishable u/Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

The 1 st Respondent being the Insurer and the 2nd & 3rd respondents being the RC owner and policy holder of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to notice issued by this tribunal, the Respondent Nos.1 to 3 appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.

5. The objections of the Respondent No.1:

sentences.text: The Driver of the Car did not have a valid DL as on the date of accident and the Car did not have a valid permit and FC.
Accordingly the police have also chargesheeted the RC owner as Accused No.2 under Sec.56 of IMV Act.
The Car not at all involved in the accident and the petitioner was riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and the accident was caused due to his own negligence.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. The objections of the Respondent Nos.2 & 3:
He has denied all the petition averments and stated that the Car was insured with the Respondent No.1 and the accident was not caused due to the negligent driving by the driver of the Car and there was negligence on the part of the petitioner himself.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

7. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 27.02.2023 at 9.30pm due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Swift D'Zire Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AH-4500 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation? If so, what is the quantum?
From whom payable?
3. What order or award?
8. The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 14 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.14.
Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. got examined as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.15 to 17.

On the other side, the Respondent No.1 has got examined its official Thrishi Subbaiah as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 & 2.
9.
Heard the arguments of the learned counsels for both the parties.

The Counsel for the petitioner has reliedupon the following decisions:
(i) 2024 ACJ 968 : Reliance Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Jotiba Shatuppa Ghadi and Ors.
(ii) 2018 ACJ 1768 : Amrit Paul Singh and Anr. Vs. Tata AIG Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., and Ors.
(iii) 2018 ACJ 2430 : Rani & orS. Vs. National Ins. Co.

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
 Issue No.1: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per the final order,
 for the following:-
 REASONS  11. Issue No.1:

In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Swift D'zire Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AH-4500 the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 7 documents as per Exs.P.1 to 7.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit in lieu of his chief examination.
During his cross-examination he has admitted that the complaint was given one day after the accident.
He has denied that the accident occurred on the extreme right side of the Road.
He has also denied that he was not wearing helmet.

As against this, the Respondent No.1 has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself and the offending insured Car did not have a valid DL and the Car did not have permit and FC.
In order to prove the same, they got examined their official as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents as per Exs.R.1 & 2, authorization letter and certified copy of policy.
During her cross-examination, she has admitted that the chargesheet was filed against the insured vehicle.
She has also admitted that the insured vehicle was used as a Cab and they had issued a policy for commercial vehicle.

She has admitted that not having permit of Car is not mentioned in the charge sheet.
12.
On perusal of the documents, it is clear that the accident occurred on 27.02.2023 at 9.30pm and the FIR was registered on 28.02.2023 at 6.00pm.
The respondent No.1 has contended that there is one day delay.
However, it is to be noted here that petitioner was taking treatment and the same thing is mentioned in the complaint annexed with the FIR at Ex.P.1.

On perusal of mahazar Ex.P.2 there is no mention of any divider but there is a divider shown in Ex.P.3 and the Sketch at Ex.P.3 which makes it clear that the petitioner was going on the extreme right side of his side of the Road whereas the offending Car came from the opposite Road and suddenly took a right.

The IMV report at Ex.P.4 shows the damages to the Cab as front bumper damaged, bonnet damaged, front right side fender damaged, front number plate damaged and the motorcycle has suffered damages to the front shape, front both side body, front suspension, front both side foot boards and head light assembly.
Therefore, it is clear that there was a head on collision.
The Wound Certificate at Ex.P.5 shows that the petitioner has suffered injuries in the RTA dated 27.02.2023.

Ex.P.6 is the ordersheet of CC 7168/2023 which was registered on the basis of the complaint at Ex.P.1 and the police after thorough investigation have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending Car as per Ex.P.7

. 
On perusal of all these documents, it is clear that there was negligence on the part of the Cab driver and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner.

Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the Ajaz Pasha vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162475652/
4 affirmative.

sentences.text: 13. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner has contended that, the petitioner has suffered injuries in the RTA.
In order to prove the same, he has produced wound certificate at Ex.P.5 which shows right femur shaft fracture which is grievous in nature.
14. In support of the same, the Petitioner got examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. as PW.2.

The Doctor has stated that the petitioner has suffered fracture of Shaft right femur in his chief-examination and has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner and has assessed the mobility and stability component and fixed the disability of the petitioner at 15.66%.

He has got marked Exs.P.15 to 17, clinical notes, case sheet and X-ray 2 in Nos.
15.
During the cross examination of PW.2, he has stated that he has personally treated the petitioner.
The fractures are united within 6 to 12 weeks.
The petitioner does not require any other treatment except the removal of implants.
The petitioner has stated that he was working as a Dry Cleaner at James Bond Dry wash company and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
As a Dry Cleaner the petitioner has to stand for a long time.
From the evidence of PW.2 it can be seen that the disability being suffered by the petitioner will impact his work.
Therefore, the court deems it fit to fix the functional disability at 15%.

Monthly income:
16.
The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was working as a Dry Cleaner at James Bond Company and getting salary of Rs.30,000/- per month.
In this regard he has not produced any documents such as Bank statement or any other documents in support of it and also not examined his employer also.
The accident occurred in the year 2023.
Therefore, this Tribunal deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.16,000/- per month.
17. At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 41 years as could be made out from Ex.P.12/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card.
He was hale and healthy before the accident.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:-

After the accident, the Petitioner was initially treated at Medax Hospital and thereafter shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bangalore, treated as an inpatient from 28.02.2023 to 06.03.2023,
discharged with advice to take follow up treatment.
In this regard, he has produced Ex.P.8 Discharge summary of Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics.

ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

sentences.text: The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards hospitalization, medical expenses, extra nourishment, conveyance and other miscellaneous expenses etc.,
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.13 for a um of Rs.26,430/-.
There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under this head.

iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner has taken treatment for 7 days at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital which can be made out from Ex.P.8 Discharge summary.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least one month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.16,000/- under this head.

iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:-
On perusal of Ex.P.12/Aadhar Card, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01.01.1983 and the date of accident is 28.02.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 40 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 15.
As such the petitioner is entitled to Rs.4,32,000/-.

(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:-
The Petitioner was aged about 40 years at the time of accident.

He has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 15%
functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.

Therefore,
considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.

(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted for 7 days as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/-
under this head.

(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:

sentences.text: As per the version of PW.2, the Petitioner has to undergo another surgery for removal of implants and the estimation of this surgery is around Rs.20,000/-.
In this regard neither the petitioner nor PW.2 has produced any estimation bill about further surgery.
He has admitted that he is a BPL Card Holder.

As per the evidence of Pws.1 & 2 and looking at the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and the evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.10,000/- is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- under this head.

18. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.80,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs.26,430/-
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.16,000/- period 4. Loss of future income Rs.4,32,400/-
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/- happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/- nourishment charges 7.

Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000/-
TOTAL Rs.6,14,430/-

If it is rounded off it comes to around Rs.6,14,500/-
and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner.
LIABILITY 19.
The respondent No.1 has contended that the offending Car did not have a valid FC and permit.

As against this, The Counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the following decisions:
(i) 2024 ACJ 968 : Reliance Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Jotiba Shatuppa Ghadi and Ors.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that in case of the offending vehicle not having a valid FC, the insurance company cannot avoid its liability on that ground alone.

sentences.text:
. 
In both the Cases, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that in case of the insured vehicle not having a Permit the Tribunal can order for Pay and Recovery.
Therefore, it is clear that even in case of absence of permit, the insurance company can be ordered for pay and recovery.
The petitioner's counsel has also furnished a copy of Permit and the DL relating to the Driver of the Cab.
The offence alleged against the owner of the vehicle in charge sheet produced at Ex.P.7 is that the vehicle does not have a FC.
But as held in the first decision, on the ground of not having FC the insurance company cannot avoid its liability.
Therefore, the said contention is rejected.
The respondent insurance company has not shown by producing any documents that the Cab did not have a valid permit.
The charge sheet does not mention about the Cab not having permit.

Therefore, the Respondent No.1 being the insurer, Respondent No.2 being the RC owner and the Respondent No.3 being the policy holder of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.6,14,500/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.

Accordingly,
I answer Issue No.2 in the affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this court proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.6,14,500/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Fourteen Thousand and Five Hundred only) from the Respondents along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.1/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
